raw_response:
I farm only 5 mu, so I cannot take big risks. For my land here in Quzhou, wheat and maize together are the safest way. Wheat gives me steady grain, and maize follows right after, so even if one season is not very good, I still have the other. I finished many years this way, so this year I will mostly follow what has worked on my fields before, with a little adjustment on fertilizer and water depending on how the crop looks. I have well water, but pumping costs money, so I will not irrigate too freely. My family has 5 people, but some work off-farm, so at busy times I need the work to be simple and on time.

For wheat, I will sow in early October with a common improved variety that local dealers sell and most neighbors use. I usually put base fertilizer before sowing, then topdress once when the wheat starts standing up strong in spring. If the leaves stay pale, I may add a bit more nitrogen, but I do not want to spend too much at once. For maize, the turn after wheat is very tight, so I will harvest wheat and plant maize immediately, with simple rotary tillage or direct seeding if I can get the machine in time. Maize usually gets one base fertilizer and one topdress around jointing. If rain is decent, I will save one irrigation. If it turns dry, I will irrigate at the key stage instead of early just to save pumping money.
